ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $\odot O$ is the circumcircle of $\triangle ABC$, where the diameter $BD$ intersects $AC$ at point E. A tangent to $\odot O$ through point D intersects the extension of $BC$ at point F, with $\angle F=\angle BAC$. Given $DF\parallel AC$, $AB = 8$, and $CF = 2$, what is the length of $AC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Draw $CD$,\\
$\because DF\parallel AC$ and $\angle ODF=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle BEC=\angle ODF=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ diameter $BD\perp AC$ at E,\\
$\therefore AE=CE=\frac{1}{2}AC$,\\
$\therefore AB=BC=8$,\\
$\because BD$ is the diameter of $\odot O$,\\
$\therefore \angle BCD=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle DBC+\angle BDC=90^\circ$,\\
$\because \angle DBC+\angle F=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle BDC=\angle F$,\\
$\because \angle BCD=\angle FCD=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \triangle BCD\sim \triangle DCF$,\\
$\therefore \frac{BC}{DC}=\frac{DC}{CF}$, i.e., $\frac{8}{DC}=\frac{DC}{2}$,\\
$\therefore DC=4$,\\
$\therefore BD=\sqrt{BC^2+CD^2}=\sqrt{8^2+4^2}=4\sqrt{5}$,\\
$\because$ in $\triangle BCD$, $S_{\triangle BCD}=\frac{1}{2}BC\cdot CD=\frac{1}{2}BD\cdot CE$,\\
$\therefore \frac{1}{2}\times 8\times 4=\frac{1}{2}\times 4\sqrt{5}\cdot CE$,\\
$\therefore CE=\frac{8}{5}\sqrt{5}$,\\
$\therefore AC=2CE=\boxed{\frac{16}{5}\sqrt{5}}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a circle, with the center of the circle labeled O. Points A, B, and C are on the circle and form triangle ABC, where B is at the lower left, A is above, and C is at the lower right. Segment BD passes through the center O, so BD is a diameter, and it intersects chord AC at point E. Point D is on the right-side circumference of the circle; from D, a tangent DF is drawn toward the lower right, and this tangent intersects the extension of BC at F. In the figure, BC and CF are on the same straight line, and DF and AC appear parallel; CD needs to be connected according to the problem statement. Reasoning: Connect CD. Because DF is the tangent to circle O at point D, and OD is on diameter BD, OD ⟂ DF, that is, BD ⟂ DF. Also because DF ∥ AC, BD ⟂ AC, with the intersection point being E, so ∠BEC=90°. The diameter BD is perpendicular to chord AC, so it bisects chord AC; hence AE=CE=AC/2. Thus B is on the perpendicular bisector of AC, so BA=BC. Given AB=8, therefore BC=8. Because BD is a diameter of circle O and C is on the circle, by the theorem that the inscribed angle subtended by a diameter is a right angle, ∠BCD=90°. Also B, C, and F are collinear, so CF and CB are on the same straight line; therefore ∠DCF=90°. In right triangle BCD, ∠DBC+∠BDC=90°. On the other hand, BD ⟂ DF, and BC and CF are collinear, so the angle formed by line BC and BD plus the angle formed by line BC and DF is 90°, that is, ∠DBC+∠F=90°. Therefore ∠BDC=∠F. Combined with ∠BCD=∠DCF=90°, we get △BCD ∼ △DCF. From the similar triangles, BC/DC = DC/CF, so DC^2=BC·CF=8×2=16; hence DC=4. Thus, in right triangle BCD, BD=√(BC^2+DC^2)=√(8^2+4^2)=√80=4√5. Because E is the intersection point of AC and BD and BD ⟂ AC, CE is the altitude from C to the hypotenuse BD in triangle BCD. Using area calculation: S△BCD=(1/2)BC·DC=(1/2)BD·CE. Substituting the numerical values gives (1/2)×8×4=(1/2)×4√5×CE, so CE=8/√5=8√5/5. Also AE=CE, so AC=2CE=16√5/5.
